title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) practice questions

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A startup expects website traffic to swing from a few hundred visitors to tens of thousands during product launches. It does not want to buy servers for the peak. Which cloud benefit addresses this most directly?
options: Elasticity, so capacity grows and shrinks with demand
High availability through a single large server
Economies of scale passed on as a fixed annual fee
Global reach through private leased lines
questions.correct_rationale: Elasticity lets the company add capacity for launch peaks and release it afterwards, paying only for what it uses.
questions.distractor_summary: A single large server is still sized for the peak and is not highly available. Economies of scale lower unit prices but are not a fixed fee. Global reach is about Regions and edge locations, not traffic swings.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which statement best describes the cloud benefit of trading fixed expense for variable expense?
options: You sign a fixed three-year contract for every service you use
You pay the same monthly price regardless of how much you use
You must buy hardware before you can use any managed service
You pay for resources as you consume them instead of buying data centers and servers up front
questions.correct_rationale: Moving to the cloud replaces large capital purchases with pay-as-you-go spending that follows actual usage.
questions.distractor_summary: Multi-year contracts and flat monthly prices are fixed costs. Managed services do not require customers to buy hardware.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company's developers wait six weeks for new test servers to be ordered and installed. Which AWS Cloud benefit would shorten this most?
options: Stop guessing capacity, because servers are always the same size
Go global in minutes, because every Region has the same services
Increased speed and agility, because resources can be provisioned in minutes
Benefit from massive economies of scale, because prices only go down
questions.correct_rationale: On demand provisioning lets teams create test environments in minutes rather than waiting for procurement.
questions.distractor_summary: Not guessing capacity is about sizing, not lead time. Going global concerns deploying in many Regions. Economies of scale concern unit prices.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: What does "stop guessing capacity" mean as a benefit of the AWS Cloud?
options: AWS chooses the right instance size for every workload automatically
You can scale resources up or down based on actual demand instead of predicting it in advance
Capacity limits do not exist in the cloud
You never need to monitor how much capacity you use
questions.correct_rationale: In the cloud you can match capacity to real demand and adjust it, so you avoid over or under buying hardware.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS does not size every workload for you, service quotas do exist, and monitoring is still needed to scale well.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A media company wants to launch its streaming app in Europe and Asia next month with low latency for local users. It has no data centers outside North America. Which cloud benefit helps most?
options: Trade fixed expense for variable expense by using Reserved Instances
Go global in minutes by deploying in AWS Regions close to those users
Increase speed and agility by using a larger instance type
Stop guessing capacity by turning on detailed monitoring
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Regions on several continents let the company deploy near its new users quickly without building data centers.
questions.distractor_summary: Reserved Instances are a pricing choice, larger instances do not reduce distance to users, and monitoring does not create a presence in new geographies.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Why can AWS often offer lower prices than a company running its own data center?
options: Its very large aggregate usage creates economies of scale
It runs older hardware that costs less to buy
It charges only for data stored, never for compute
It shares each customer's servers with no isolation
questions.correct_rationale: Aggregated usage across many customers lets AWS buy and run infrastructure more cheaply per unit and pass savings on.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS does not rely on outdated hardware, compute is billed, and customer workloads are isolated.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A finance manager asks how moving to AWS changes how the company spends money on infrastructure. Which answer is most accurate?
options: All spending becomes capital expense that can be depreciated over five years
Infrastructure becomes free after the first year
Costs become fixed and cannot change month to month
Less money goes to upfront capital purchases and more to operating expenses that follow usage
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud spending is mainly operating expense based on consumption, rather than large capital purchases.
questions.distractor_summary: Cloud usage is not capital expense, there is no general free-after-one-year rule, and costs vary with use.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the agility benefit of the cloud?
options: A team signs a five-year hosting contract to lock in a price
A team buys spare servers in case demand grows next year
A team experiments with a new database engine for a day and deletes it when the test ends
A team keeps every environment running all year in case it is needed
questions.correct_rationale: Agility means you can try things quickly and cheaply, then throw them away, because resources are on demand.
questions.distractor_summary: Long contracts, spare hardware, and always-on environments are the opposite of agile, low-risk experimentation.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework focuses on the ability of a workload to recover from failures and meet demand?
questions.correct_rationale: The Reliability pillar covers recovering from infrastructure or service disruptions and acquiring resources to meet demand.
questions.distractor_summary: Performance efficiency is about using resources efficiently, cost optimization about avoiding unnecessary cost, and sustainability about reducing environmental impact.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: How many pillars does the AWS Well-Architected Framework have?
questions.correct_rationale: The pillars are operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.
questions.distractor_summary: Five was the count before the sustainability pillar was added; four and seven are not correct.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: An architect wants every part of a system to be able to fail without taking down the whole application. Which design principle is she applying?
options: Design for failure and remove single points of failure
Use the largest possible instance types
Keep all components on one server to reduce network hops
Disable automatic scaling to keep behavior predictable
questions.correct_rationale: Designing for failure assumes components will break and adds redundancy so no single failure stops the system.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger instances and single servers still fail as a unit, and disabling scaling reduces resilience.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which design principle describes breaking an application into smaller components that communicate through queues or APIs so they can scale and fail independently?
questions.correct_rationale: Loosely coupled components reduce dependencies, so one part can slow down or fail without stopping the others.
questions.distractor_summary: Vertical scaling makes one server bigger, tight integration increases dependencies, and lift and shift is a migration approach.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A team manually changes server settings through the console, and environments keep drifting apart. Which Well-Architected operational excellence practice fits best?
options: Give every engineer full administrator access to fix drift quickly
Make large changes once a year to reduce the number of deployments
Stop using automation so each change is reviewed by hand
Perform operations as code, for example with infrastructure as code templates
questions.correct_rationale: Defining infrastructure and operations as code makes changes repeatable and reviewable, which prevents drift.
questions.distractor_summary: Broad admin access and manual changes increase drift, and large infrequent changes raise risk instead of reducing it.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which pillar of the Well-Architected Framework includes the principle "apply security at all layers"?
questions.correct_rationale: Applying defense in depth across network, compute, application, and data layers is a Security pillar principle.
questions.distractor_summary: The other pillars cover running workloads, recovering from failure, and using resources efficiently.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company wants to reduce the energy its workloads use by choosing efficient instance types and removing idle resources. Which pillar provides guidance for this goal?
questions.correct_rationale: The Sustainability pillar focuses on minimizing environmental impact, including maximizing utilization and choosing efficient hardware.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost optimization overlaps in practice but its goal is cost, not environmental impact. Reliability and operational excellence have different goals.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which practice best reflects the performance efficiency principle "use serverless architectures"?
options: Running code in AWS Lambda so you do not manage servers for event-driven tasks
Running a fleet of always-on instances sized for peak load
Buying dedicated hosts for every application
Moving every workload to the largest available Region
questions.correct_rationale: Serverless services remove server management and scale automatically, letting you focus on the workload.
questions.distractor_summary: Always-on peak-sized fleets and dedicated hosts add management, and Region size is not a serverless concept.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: An application stores session data on each web server, so users lose their sessions when a server is replaced. Which design change best supports horizontal scaling?
options: Store session state outside the web servers, for example in Amazon ElastiCache or DynamoDB
Use a bigger web server so it is replaced less often
Disable Auto Scaling so servers are never replaced
Store sessions on the local disk of each server with larger volumes
questions.correct_rationale: Keeping servers stateless lets any server handle any request, so servers can be added or removed freely.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger or never-replaced servers avoid the design problem rather than solve it, and local disks keep the state tied to one server.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which pillar includes the design principle "stop spending money on undifferentiated heavy lifting"?
questions.correct_rationale: Using managed services so your team does not run data centers or routine infrastructure is a cost optimization principle.
questions.distractor_summary: The other pillars focus on protection, resilience, and environmental impact.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which AWS framework helps organizations plan cloud adoption across business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations perspectives?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS CAF organizes adoption guidance into six perspectives so organizations can plan the capabilities they need.
questions.distractor_summary: The Well-Architected Framework reviews workload design, the shared responsibility model divides security duties, and the Pricing Calculator estimates costs.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on organizational change management, culture, and cloud skills?
questions.correct_rationale: The People perspective covers culture, organizational structure, leadership, and workforce skills for the cloud.
questions.distractor_summary: Platform covers architecture, Security covers protection, and Operations covers running services.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company plans to move a legacy application to AWS as quickly as possible with no code changes. Which migration strategy is this?
options: Rehost, often called lift and shift
questions.correct_rationale: Rehosting moves the application as it is, which is usually the fastest approach.
questions.distractor_summary: Refactoring changes the code, repurchasing moves to a different product such as SaaS, and retiring turns the application off.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company will replace its on-premises CRM software with a software as a service CRM product. Which migration strategy is this?
questions.correct_rationale: Repurchasing means moving to a different product, often SaaS, instead of migrating the existing software.
questions.distractor_summary: Rehosting and replatforming move the current application, and retaining keeps it where it is.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: During migration planning, a team moves its database to Amazon RDS but leaves the application code unchanged apart from the connection string. Which strategy is this?
questions.correct_rationale: Replatforming makes a few cloud optimizations, such as a managed database, without changing the core architecture.
questions.distractor_summary: Rehost keeps everything the same, refactor redesigns the application, and relocate moves a platform such as VMware to the cloud.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which AWS service helps discover on-premises servers and track migration progress across tools in one place?
questions.correct_rationale: Migration Hub gives a single place to discover servers, plan migrations, and track their status.
questions.distractor_summary: Snowball Edge moves data physically, CloudFront is a content delivery network, and Budgets tracks spending.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company has 400 TB of archive data to move to Amazon S3, and its internet link would take months. Which service fits best?
options: AWS Direct Connect set up for a one-time copy over the internet
Amazon CloudFront to upload the files faster
AWS Snowball Edge devices shipped to the data center
questions.correct_rationale: Snowball Edge devices move large amounts of data offline when network transfer would take too long.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct Connect is a dedicated link that takes time to provision and is not an internet copy tool, CloudFront delivers content to users, and DMS migrates databases.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which migration strategy means deciding to keep an application on premises for now?
questions.correct_rationale: Retaining means the application stays where it is, often because it is not ready or not worth moving yet.
questions.distractor_summary: Retiring shuts the application down, rehosting moves it, and repurchasing replaces it with another product.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company wants to migrate a self-managed Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with minimal downtime. Which combination of AWS services helps most?
options: AWS Schema Conversion Tool and AWS Database Migration Service
AWS DataSync and Amazon S3 Glacier
AWS Backup and Amazon EBS snapshots
questions.correct_rationale: The Schema Conversion Tool converts the schema to the new engine, and DMS moves and keeps data in sync to limit downtime.
questions.distractor_summary: DataSync copies files and Glacier stores archives, so neither converts database engines, CloudWatch and Config are monitoring and compliance tools, and Backup with snapshots does not convert engines.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 Understand the benefits of and strategies for migration to the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which is a common business benefit of migrating to the AWS Cloud cited in AWS CAF?
options: Elimination of all security responsibilities for the customer
Guaranteed lower costs for every workload without changes
Removal of the need for any IT staff
Reduced business risk, improved operational efficiency, and faster innovation
questions.correct_rationale: AWS CAF describes outcomes such as reduced risk, better efficiency, and increased revenue through faster innovation.
questions.distractor_summary: Customers keep security responsibilities, savings depend on how workloads are run, and IT skills are still needed.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which cost is usually lower in the cloud than on premises because AWS manages the physical infrastructure?
options: Software licenses that you bring yourself
Staff time to design your application
Training your developers on your own code
Data center power, cooling, and hardware maintenance
questions.correct_rationale: AWS runs the physical facilities, so customers no longer pay directly for power, cooling, and hardware upkeep.
questions.distractor_summary: Licenses you bring, application design, and internal training remain the customer's costs.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company compares running its own servers with AWS. Which item belongs in a total cost of ownership (TCO) comparison but is easy to forget?
options: The color of the server racks
The number of AWS Regions in the world
Staff time for patching, hardware refresh, and data center operations
The name of the cloud provider's CEO
questions.correct_rationale: TCO includes indirect costs such as people, facilities, and refresh cycles, not just the server price.
questions.distractor_summary: The other items have no effect on cost.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: What is right sizing?
options: Always choosing the largest instance to avoid performance problems
Matching instance types and sizes to the actual workload requirements to avoid paying for unused capacity
Buying exactly one instance per application
Choosing the Region with the most Availability Zones
questions.correct_rationale: Right sizing uses monitoring data to choose instance types and sizes that fit the workload, reducing waste.
questions.distractor_summary: Oversizing wastes money, one instance per application is not a sizing method, and Region choice is a separate decision.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company moving to AWS wants to reuse its existing Microsoft Windows Server licenses where permitted. What concept is this?
questions.correct_rationale: BYOL lets customers apply eligible licenses they already own, which can lower cost on AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: License-included instances bundle the license cost, Spot is a compute pricing model, and the free tier is a limited trial allowance.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which statement about cloud economics is accurate?
options: Automating infrastructure can reduce operational costs such as manual administration
Moving to the cloud always halves costs regardless of design
The cloud has no ongoing costs after migration
On-premises servers have no hidden costs
questions.correct_rationale: Automation reduces labor and errors, which lowers ongoing operational costs.
questions.distractor_summary: Savings depend on design and usage, cloud usage has ongoing costs, and on-premises environments have hidden costs such as facilities.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A CFO notices that the monthly AWS bill grows each month even though usage is flat. A review finds many unattached EBS volumes and idle instances. Which economic concept does this show?
options: AWS raises prices automatically each month
Pay-as-you-go pricing is only for the first year
Cloud economics do not apply to storage
Cloud costs depend on governance; unused resources keep costing money until removed
questions.correct_rationale: Resources are billed while they exist, so idle and orphaned resources need to be found and deleted.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS does not raise prices monthly, pay-as-you-go continues, and storage is billed like other resources.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which is an example of the cloud reducing the cost of failed experiments?
options: A team buys servers for a prototype and keeps them after it fails
A team signs a long contract before testing an idea
A team builds a prototype, finds it does not work, and deletes it after paying only for a few hours of use
A team builds a data center for testing
questions.correct_rationale: Because you only pay while resources exist, failed experiments cost little and can be shut down.
questions.distractor_summary: Buying hardware, long contracts, and building facilities make failed experiments expensive.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company wants to estimate the monthly cost of a planned AWS architecture before building it. Which tool should it use?
questions.correct_rationale: Pricing Calculator models the cost of services you plan to use before you deploy them.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost Explorer analyzes past and current spending, Trusted Advisor checks existing resources, and Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which concept means paying a lower price per unit as you use more of a service, such as some Amazon S3 storage tiers?
questions.correct_rationale: Some services charge less per unit as usage grows beyond tier thresholds.
questions.distractor_summary: Spot is spare compute capacity, and fixed or dedicated pricing are not tiered discounts.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company keeps its test environments running nights and weekends even though nobody uses them. What cost-saving action fits cloud economics best?
options: Stop or schedule the test resources to run only during working hours
Buy Reserved Instances for the test environment
Move the test environment to a larger instance type
Copy the test environment to a second Region
questions.correct_rationale: Turning off unused resources outside working hours removes charges for idle capacity.
questions.distractor_summary: Reservations commit to always-on use, bigger instances cost more, and a second Region doubles cost.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: How does the cloud change the economics of high availability compared with a single data center?
options: High availability is free on AWS for every service
High availability is impossible to achieve in the cloud
High availability requires buying Dedicated Hosts in every Zone
Customers can use multiple Availability Zones without building and running extra facilities themselves
questions.correct_rationale: Availability Zones are already built, so redundancy costs only the resources you place in them, not new facilities.
questions.distractor_summary: Redundant resources still cost money, high availability is achievable, and Dedicated Hosts are not required.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company's on-premises servers average 15 percent utilization because they were bought for peak load. What is the main economic benefit of moving these workloads to AWS with Auto Scaling?
options: Paying a lower electricity rate for the same idle servers
Paying for capacity that tracks demand instead of idle peak capacity
Removing the need to monitor performance
questions.correct_rationale: Auto Scaling adds and removes capacity with demand, so the company stops paying for capacity that sits idle.
questions.distractor_summary: Electricity is not billed separately, licensing still applies, and monitoring is still needed.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which AWS benefit lets a company avoid paying for hardware refresh cycles every few years?
options: Customers receive new physical servers by mail each year
Hardware refresh is billed as a separate fee every three years
AWS replaces and upgrades the underlying hardware as part of the service
questions.correct_rationale: AWS maintains and refreshes physical infrastructure, so customers do not run refresh projects.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS does not ship servers to customers, there is no refresh fee, and reservations do not transfer ownership.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company's analysis shows that moving a workload to AWS saves money only if it changes from a fixed fleet to on-demand scaling. What does this tell the company about cloud economics?
options: Moving servers as they are always gives the highest savings
Savings come from adapting architecture and operations, not just from moving servers as they are
On-demand scaling increases costs in every case
Cloud savings depend only on the Region chosen
questions.correct_rationale: Optimizing workloads for the cloud, such as scaling with demand, is often where the largest savings come from.
questions.distractor_summary: Lift and shift alone may not save much, scaling usually reduces waste, and Region is only one factor.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: What is the AWS Free Tier?
options: A limited allowance of certain services that new and existing customers can use at no charge within set limits
A permanent unlimited free plan for all services
A discount for customers who sign a three-year contract
A support plan with a technical account manager
questions.correct_rationale: The Free Tier offers free trials, short-term free usage, and always-free limits on specific services.
questions.distractor_summary: It is limited, not unlimited, and it is not a contract discount or a support plan.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A company wants to understand how much of its IT budget would change if it moved to AWS, including staffing and facilities. What kind of analysis is this?
options: A total cost of ownership comparison
questions.correct_rationale: TCO analysis compares all direct and indirect costs of running on premises versus in the cloud.
questions.distractor_summary: Penetration tests and disaster recovery drills are operational activities, and security reviews do not model budgets.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which pricing benefit is gained by using managed services such as Amazon RDS instead of self-managed databases on EC2?
options: Free database storage with no limit
Lower operational overhead because AWS handles tasks such as patching and backups
questions.correct_rationale: Managed services shift routine administration to AWS, reducing the staff time the customer spends.
questions.distractor_summary: Storage and instances are still billed, and there are no refunds for query speed.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: A small company has no idea how much traffic its new app will get. Which pricing approach reduces its financial risk at launch?
options: Buying a rack of servers for the expected peak
On-demand, pay-as-you-go pricing with no long-term commitment
questions.correct_rationale: Without commitments, the company pays only for what it uses while learning its real demand.
questions.distractor_summary: Long commitments and hardware purchases lock in spending before demand is known.

questions.subdomain: 1.4 Understand concepts of cloud economics
questions.question: Which statement about the economics of scale on AWS is accurate?
options: AWS prices are fixed by law and never change
AWS has historically reduced prices over time as its scale and efficiency grew
Customers pay more per unit as AWS grows larger
Economies of scale only apply to customers with dedicated hardware
questions.correct_rationale: AWS has passed efficiency gains to customers through many price reductions over the years.
questions.distractor_summary: Prices are not fixed by law, per-unit prices have trended down, and the benefit applies broadly.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 Identify design principles of the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A team wants to roll out changes in small, frequent, reversible steps so a bad change affects few users. Which Well-Architected operational excellence principle is this?
options: Make large changes during annual maintenance windows
Avoid changes once the system is in production
Test changes only after they reach all users
questions.correct_rationale: Small reversible changes limit the blast radius of mistakes and are easy to roll back.
questions.distractor_summary: Large infrequent changes increase risk, freezing production prevents improvement, and testing after full rollout exposes every user.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the physical security of AWS data centers?
options: An independent auditor chosen by the customer
questions.correct_rationale: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes physical facilities.
questions.distractor_summary: Customers are responsible for security in the cloud, not the buildings; providers and auditors do not run AWS facilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: Which task is the customer's responsibility when using Amazon EC2?
options: Replacing failed physical disks in the host
questions.correct_rationale: With EC2 the customer manages the guest OS, including updates and security patches.
questions.distractor_summary: Physical disks, the hypervisor, and cooling are AWS responsibilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: A company moves a self-managed MySQL database from EC2 to Amazon RDS. Which responsibility shifts from the customer to AWS?
options: Deciding which users can connect to the database
Classifying the data stored in the database
Patching the database engine and underlying operating system
Configuring security group rules for the database
questions.correct_rationale: With RDS, AWS manages the OS and database engine patching, while the customer still controls access and data.
questions.distractor_summary: Database users, data classification, and security groups remain customer responsibilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: In the shared responsibility model, which responsibility is shared between AWS and the customer?
options: Patch management, because AWS patches the infrastructure and the customer patches its guest OS and applications
Management of the global network backbone
questions.correct_rationale: Patch management is a shared control: each party patches the layers it controls.
questions.distractor_summary: Facilities, the backbone, and media destruction are AWS-only responsibilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: A customer uses AWS Lambda. Which item is still the customer's responsibility?
options: Patching the operating system that runs the function
The function code and the IAM permissions it uses
Scaling the servers that run the function
questions.correct_rationale: With Lambda, AWS runs and patches the infrastructure, but the customer owns its code, configuration, and permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: OS patching, scaling, and hardware are handled by AWS for Lambda.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: How does the customer's share of responsibility change as it moves from Amazon EC2 to AWS Lambda?
options: It gets smaller, because AWS manages more of the stack
It gets larger, because serverless is harder to secure
It stays exactly the same for every service
questions.correct_rationale: Higher-level managed services shift more operational security tasks to AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: Responsibility does not grow, it varies by service, and the customer always keeps data and access responsibilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: A company accidentally makes an Amazon S3 bucket public, and data is exposed. Under the shared responsibility model, whose responsibility was this configuration?
options: AWS's, because S3 is a managed service
Both equally, with AWS paying for any loss
Nobody's, because S3 is public by default
The customer's, because it controls bucket permissions
questions.correct_rationale: Customers configure access to their data, including bucket policies and public access settings.
questions.distractor_summary: S3 being managed does not move access decisions to AWS, and new buckets block public access by default.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: Which is an AWS responsibility under the shared responsibility model?
options: Encrypting customer data in every case
Creating IAM users for the customer's employees
Protecting the infrastructure that runs AWS services
Writing the customer's security group rules
questions.correct_rationale: AWS secures the hardware, software, networking, and facilities that run its services.
questions.distractor_summary: Encryption choices, IAM users, and security groups are configured by the customer.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: A customer asks who is responsible for training its staff to handle data securely in AWS. What is the correct answer?
options: AWS, because it runs the cloud
AWS Support, through every support plan
The customer, because awareness and training are customer-specific controls
The AWS Partner who sold the account
questions.correct_rationale: Customer-specific controls such as staff training are the customer's responsibility.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS trains its own employees, not customers' staff, and support plans and partners do not take on this duty.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 Understand the AWS shared responsibility model
questions.question: For Amazon DynamoDB, which task does AWS handle?
options: Choosing which IAM principals can read a table
Operating and patching the underlying servers and storage
Deciding whether to enable point-in-time recovery
Classifying the sensitivity of stored items
questions.correct_rationale: DynamoDB is fully managed, so AWS operates the infrastructure.
questions.distractor_summary: Access, backup settings, and data classification are customer choices.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Where can a customer download AWS compliance reports such as SOC reports and ISO certifications?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and agreements.
questions.distractor_summary: Config tracks resource configuration, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: An auditor asks for evidence that AWS data centers meet a recognized security standard. What should the company provide?
options: A screenshot of the AWS console home page
The company's own data center policy
The relevant AWS compliance report downloaded from AWS Artifact
questions.correct_rationale: Artifact supplies third-party audit reports about AWS's controls that auditors can review.
questions.distractor_summary: A console screenshot, internal policy, or cost estimate does not prove AWS's compliance.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Which AWS service continuously records resource configuration changes and evaluates them against rules?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Config records configuration history and checks resources against compliance rules.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudWatch collects metrics and logs, CloudTrail records API calls, and Artifact provides compliance documents.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Which AWS service records API calls made in an account, including who made them and when?
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail logs account activity and API calls for auditing and investigation.
questions.distractor_summary: CloudWatch focuses on metrics and logs, Config on configuration state, and GuardDuty on threat detection.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A security team wants to know which user deleted an Amazon S3 bucket yesterday. Which service should it check first?
questions.correct_rationale: CloudTrail event history shows the API call, the identity that made it, and when.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost Explorer shows spending, Inspector scans workloads, and Artifact holds compliance reports.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: What does encryption at rest protect against?
options: Exposure of stored data if storage media or snapshots are accessed without authorization
Interception of data while it travels over the network
questions.correct_rationale: Encryption at rest keeps stored data unreadable without the keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Data in transit needs TLS, weak passwords need password policies and MFA, and DDoS needs services such as AWS Shield.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A company must encrypt data moving between users' browsers and its web application. What should it use?
options: Encryption at rest on EBS volumes
questions.correct_rationale: TLS encrypts data as it travels across the network.
questions.distractor_summary: At-rest encryption protects stored data, versioning keeps object history, and budgets track spending.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Which AWS service lets customers create and control encryption keys used across many AWS services?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS KMS creates and manages cryptographic keys and integrates with many services for encryption.
questions.distractor_summary: Secrets Manager stores secrets such as passwords, Certificate Manager handles TLS certificates, and Macie discovers sensitive data.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A company must show regulators that its own AWS workloads follow its internal security policies. Which statement is accurate?
options: AWS compliance reports automatically certify every customer workload
Using AWS means the company has no compliance obligations
AWS compliance reports cover AWS's controls; the company must still show its own controls are in place
Only AWS can be audited, not the customer's resources
questions.correct_rationale: AWS's certifications cover its part of the shared model; customers prove compliance for the parts they control.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS reports do not certify customer workloads or remove customer obligations, and customer resources can be audited.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Which AWS service uses machine learning to discover and help protect sensitive data, such as personal information, stored in Amazon S3?
questions.correct_rationale: Macie finds sensitive data such as personal information in S3 and reports on data security risks.
questions.distractor_summary: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Shield protects against DDoS, and Detective helps investigate security findings.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A company must keep log files for seven years and prove they were not changed. Which approach fits best?
options: Store logs on an EC2 instance store volume
Store logs in Amazon S3 with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode and a retention period
Keep logs only in CloudWatch with the default settings
Email the logs to the auditor each month
questions.correct_rationale: Object Lock in compliance mode prevents objects from being deleted or overwritten until retention ends.
questions.distractor_summary: Instance store is temporary, default settings do not guarantee long immutable retention, and email is not a controlled archive.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: What is the purpose of the AWS Compliance Programs information on the AWS website and in AWS Artifact?
options: To show which standards and regulations AWS has been assessed against
To certify that a customer's application is compliant
To list prices for compliance-related services
To replace a customer's internal audits
questions.correct_rationale: AWS publishes the assurance programs it participates in so customers can rely on them for their part of compliance.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not certify customer apps, list prices, or replace customer audits.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A healthcare company wants to process protected health information on AWS. What is a required step it should take?
options: Assume all AWS services are automatically compliant for health data
Store all health data unencrypted for faster access
Ask AWS to manage its user permissions
Review and accept the AWS Business Associate Addendum through AWS Artifact and use eligible services
questions.correct_rationale: For US health data, customers accept the BAA and use HIPAA-eligible services configured correctly.
questions.distractor_summary: Not all services are eligible by default, unencrypted storage is a poor practice, and permissions stay with the customer.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Which service gives a central view of security findings from services such as Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, and Amazon Macie?
questions.correct_rationale: Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes security findings and checks against standards.
questions.distractor_summary: Cost Explorer covers spending, Organizations manages accounts, and Systems Manager handles operations tasks.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A company runs workloads in several AWS Regions and must keep customer data inside the European Union. Which control best helps enforce this across all accounts?
options: A note in the company wiki asking staff to use EU Regions
AWS Budgets alerts for non-EU spending
A service control policy in AWS Organizations that denies actions outside approved Regions
questions.correct_rationale: An SCP can deny API actions in Regions that are not approved, which applies to every account in the organization.
questions.distractor_summary: A wiki note is not enforced, budgets only alert on cost, and CloudFront geo restriction controls who can view content, not where data is stored.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which AWS identity has complete access to all resources in an account and should be used only for a few account tasks?
options: An IAM user with read-only permissions
An IAM role used by EC2
questions.correct_rationale: The root user has full, unrestricted access, so it should be protected with MFA and rarely used.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM users, roles, and federated users only have the permissions granted to them.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: What should a company do first to protect its AWS account root user?
options: Enable multi-factor authentication and avoid using root for everyday tasks
Share the root password with the whole IT team
Create access keys for the root user for scripts
Use the root user for daily administration
questions.correct_rationale: MFA and minimal use protect the most powerful identity in the account.
questions.distractor_summary: Sharing passwords, creating root access keys, and daily root use all increase risk.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
options: Granting administrator access to every developer
Removing all permissions from all users
Using the root user for automation
Granting only the permissions needed to perform a task
questions.correct_rationale: Least privilege limits the damage if credentials are misused by giving only what is needed.
questions.distractor_summary: Broad admin access and root automation are risky, and removing all permissions stops work.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which IAM feature lets an application on Amazon EC2 access Amazon S3 without storing access keys on the instance?
options: An IAM user with long-term access keys in a config file
An IAM role attached through an instance profile
questions.correct_rationale: Roles give the instance temporary credentials that rotate automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: Stored keys can leak, root should never be used this way, and security groups control network traffic, not API permissions.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: A company has 200 employees who already sign in to a corporate identity provider. It wants them to access several AWS accounts with single sign-on. Which service fits best?
options: Separate IAM users in each account
Amazon Cognito user pools for employees in every account
The account root user with shared passwords
questions.correct_rationale: IAM Identity Center connects to an identity provider and gives workforce users single sign-on to multiple accounts.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate IAM users are hard to manage, Cognito is aimed at customer-facing apps, and shared root passwords are unsafe.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: What is an IAM group used for?
options: Attaching permissions to many IAM users at once
Grouping S3 buckets into a single bucket
questions.correct_rationale: Groups let administrators manage permissions for a set of users by attaching policies to the group.
questions.distractor_summary: Auto Scaling groups manage instances, Organizations groups accounts, and buckets are not merged.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: A developer accidentally committed AWS access keys to a public code repository. What should be done immediately?
options: Deactivate and rotate the exposed access keys and review CloudTrail for misuse
Make the repository private and keep using the keys
Delete the repository and take no other action
Wait for AWS to delete the keys automatically
questions.correct_rationale: Exposed keys must be disabled and replaced quickly, then activity should be reviewed.
questions.distractor_summary: Keys may already be copied, so hiding or deleting the repository is not enough, and AWS does not rotate customer keys for you.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which document defines permissions in AWS IAM?
questions.correct_rationale: IAM policies are JSON documents that allow or deny actions on resources.
questions.distractor_summary: The other formats are not used to define IAM permissions.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: When an IAM policy explicitly denies an action and another policy allows it, what happens?
options: The allow wins because it is more specific
The most recently created policy wins
AWS asks the user to choose
The explicit deny wins and the action is denied
questions.correct_rationale: In IAM policy evaluation, an explicit deny always overrides an allow.
questions.distractor_summary: Specificity, creation time, and user choice do not override an explicit deny.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: A company wants to let a partner company's AWS account read objects in one of its S3 buckets without creating IAM users for the partner. Which approach fits best?
options: Email the partner the root user credentials
Create IAM users and share their passwords
Create an IAM role the partner account can assume, or grant access with a bucket policy naming the partner account
questions.correct_rationale: Cross-account roles or resource policies grant scoped access without sharing credentials.
questions.distractor_summary: Root credentials and shared passwords are unsafe, and a public bucket exposes data to everyone.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which AWS feature enforces password length and complexity rules for IAM users?
questions.correct_rationale: An IAM password policy sets complexity, length, and rotation requirements for IAM user passwords.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups, Shield, and CloudFront do not manage IAM passwords.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: An administrator wants a report listing all IAM users and the status of their passwords, access keys, and MFA devices. What should she use?
questions.correct_rationale: The credential report lists users and the status of their credentials, including MFA.
questions.distractor_summary: The other reports cover cost, vulnerabilities, and compliance documents.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: What does multi-factor authentication (MFA) add to an AWS sign-in?
options: A second proof of identity, such as a code from a device, in addition to the password
A second password that is the same as the first
questions.correct_rationale: MFA requires something you have in addition to something you know, making stolen passwords less useful.
questions.distractor_summary: Repeating a password adds nothing, and MFA does not encrypt data or change permissions.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which feature gives temporary, limited-privilege credentials to a user or service?
options: AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) through role assumption
questions.correct_rationale: STS issues temporary credentials when a role is assumed, which expire automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: Long-term keys and the root password do not expire, and ACLs grant object permissions rather than credentials.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which tool helps identify resources in an account that are shared with external principals, such as buckets or roles accessible from outside the organization?
questions.correct_rationale: IAM Access Analyzer reviews resource policies to find access granted to external principals.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools are for cost, log queries, and estimates.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Which AWS service provides managed protection against distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks and is included at no extra cost for all customers at the standard level?
questions.correct_rationale: Shield Standard is automatically included and protects against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield Advanced is a paid upgrade, WAF filters web requests, and GuardDuty detects threats.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Which AWS service filters web requests to protect applications from common exploits such as SQL injection?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS WAF lets you create rules that block malicious web requests to CloudFront, load balancers, and API Gateway.
questions.distractor_summary: Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, Shield protects against DDoS, and Config tracks configuration.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: A company wants continuous threat detection that analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs for suspicious activity. Which service should it enable?
questions.correct_rationale: GuardDuty uses threat intelligence and anomaly detection on these data sources to report findings.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact holds compliance reports, Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks, and Macie focuses on sensitive data in S3.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Which AWS service automatically scans EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities?
questions.correct_rationale: Inspector discovers workloads and scans them for known vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.
questions.distractor_summary: GuardDuty detects threats, Shield handles DDoS, and Secrets Manager stores secrets.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Developers store database passwords in application code. Which service should they use to store and rotate these credentials securely?
questions.correct_rationale: Secrets Manager stores secrets encrypted and can rotate them automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: Public buckets expose data, CloudFront delivers content, and Budgets tracks costs.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: What does a security group do?
options: Groups IAM users who share permissions
Acts as a stateful virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic for resources such as EC2 instances
Protects against DDoS attacks at the edge
questions.correct_rationale: Security groups control traffic at the resource level, and return traffic is allowed automatically because they are stateful.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM groups manage permissions, KMS handles encryption, and Shield protects against DDoS.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: How is a network ACL different from a security group?
options: A network ACL is attached to each instance and is stateful
A network ACL works at the subnet level and is stateless, so return traffic must be allowed explicitly
A network ACL only filters traffic from the internet to S3
A network ACL encrypts traffic between subnets
questions.correct_rationale: Network ACLs filter traffic entering and leaving subnets, and they evaluate inbound and outbound rules separately.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups attach to instances and are stateful, ACLs are not specific to S3, and they do not encrypt.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: A company wants a checklist that compares its account settings with security best practices, such as open ports and MFA on the root user. Which service provides these checks?
questions.correct_rationale: Trusted Advisor inspects the account and recommends improvements in security, cost, performance, and more.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact is for compliance documents, Detective for investigations, and Snowball for data transfer.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Which AWS service issues and manages TLS certificates for use with services such as Elastic Load Balancing and CloudFront?
questions.correct_rationale: Certificate Manager provisions, manages, and renews public and private TLS certificates.
questions.distractor_summary: KMS manages encryption keys, Secrets Manager stores secrets, and Artifact provides reports.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: A security team has dozens of GuardDuty findings and needs to understand how a suspicious IP address interacted with its resources over the past weeks. Which service helps with this investigation?
questions.correct_rationale: Detective builds a linked view of activity from logs so analysts can investigate the scope and root cause of findings.
questions.distractor_summary: Config tracks configuration, Budgets tracks spending, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Where can customers find security best practices, whitepapers, and guidance from AWS?
options: Only by opening a paid support case
The AWS Security Center, AWS documentation, and the AWS Knowledge Center
questions.correct_rationale: AWS publishes security guidance publicly through its security resources, documentation, and knowledge base.
questions.distractor_summary: Guidance is freely available, not only through paid support or partners, and Cost Explorer is a cost tool.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: A company wants third-party security software, such as a next-generation firewall, that runs in its AWS account. Where can it find and buy such products?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Marketplace offers third-party software, including security products, that can be deployed in AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact provides compliance documents, Trusted Advisor gives checks, and the Health Dashboard reports service events.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Which service helps centrally manage firewall rules, including AWS WAF rules and security groups, across many accounts in AWS Organizations?
questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Manager applies and monitors firewall policies consistently across accounts in an organization.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield Standard is automatic DDoS protection, Inspector scans vulnerabilities, and Artifact provides reports.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: A company wants to see whether any of its AWS services are affected by an ongoing AWS event, such as a Regional issue. Where should it look?
questions.correct_rationale: The Health Dashboard shows AWS service events and account-specific issues that may affect your resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact holds compliance reports, the Pricing Calculator estimates costs, and Macie finds sensitive data.

questions.subdomain: 2.4 Identify components and resources for security
questions.question: Which AWS Shield tier adds 24/7 access to the AWS Shield Response Team and cost protection for scaling during attacks?
questions.correct_rationale: Shield Advanced is a paid tier that adds expert response support, enhanced detection, and DDoS cost protection.
questions.distractor_summary: Shield Standard is the free baseline, WAF filters web requests, and GuardDuty detects threats.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: A company needs a record of every configuration change to its security groups so it can review changes over the past year. Which service fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: AWS Config keeps a configuration history for supported resources, including security groups.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact provides reports, Budgets tracks spending, and Polly converts text to speech.

questions.subdomain: 2.2 Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
questions.question: Which statement about encryption options in AWS is accurate?
options: AWS never allows customers to manage their own keys
Encryption is only available for Amazon S3
Many AWS services offer encryption at rest that customers can turn on, often using keys from AWS KMS
Encryption makes data unavailable to the customer
questions.correct_rationale: Most storage and database services support encryption at rest integrated with KMS, including customer managed keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Customers can manage keys, encryption is widely available, and authorized users can still read encrypted data.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: A team wants an IAM role that developers assume to deploy to production, but only when they sign in with MFA. How can this be enforced?
options: Create a security group that requires MFA
Add a condition to the role's trust policy that requires MFA to be present
Turn on Shield Advanced for the account
Store the role ARN in Secrets Manager
questions.correct_rationale: IAM policy conditions such as aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent can require MFA before a role can be assumed.
questions.distractor_summary: Security groups, Shield, and Secrets Manager do not control role assumption.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: Which type of policy is attached directly to a resource, such as an S3 bucket, to grant access?
options: An identity-based policy attached to a user
questions.correct_rationale: Resource-based policies are attached to resources and specify which principals can access them.
questions.distractor_summary: Identity-based policies attach to users, groups, or roles; SCPs and permissions boundaries set maximum permissions.

questions.subdomain: 2.3 Identify AWS access management capabilities
questions.question: A company's security officer wants to limit what even administrators in member accounts can do, such as stopping them from disabling CloudTrail. Which feature fits best?
options: Service control policies in AWS Organizations
questions.correct_rationale: SCPs set the maximum permissions for accounts in an organization, including for administrators.
questions.distractor_summary: IAM groups grant permissions within one account, Budgets actions respond to spend, and bucket policies protect buckets.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which are the main ways to access and manage AWS services?
options: The AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, and the AWS SDKs or APIs
questions.correct_rationale: AWS can be managed through the web console, the command line, and programmatically through SDKs and APIs.
questions.distractor_summary: The console is not the only option, and Support and Marketplace are not management interfaces.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company wants to define its whole AWS environment in templates so it can recreate it consistently. Which service fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: CloudFormation provisions resources from templates, making environments repeatable.
questions.distractor_summary: Artifact holds compliance reports, Connect is a contact center service, and Budgets tracks spending.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which deployment model connects on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources so they work together?
questions.correct_rationale: A hybrid model combines on-premises environments with cloud services.
questions.distractor_summary: Public or private cloud alone does not connect both, and SaaS is a service model, not a connectivity model.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A developer wants to write Python code that creates S3 buckets and launches EC2 instances. What should she use?
questions.correct_rationale: The AWS SDKs let programs call AWS APIs in languages such as Python.
questions.distractor_summary: The other tools estimate costs, provide reports, or show service health.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which AWS service lets developers upload application code and have AWS handle capacity provisioning, load balancing, and scaling for web applications?
questions.correct_rationale: Elastic Beanstalk deploys and manages web applications while you keep control of the underlying resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers, Snowball Edge moves data, and Redshift is a data warehouse.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company needs a browser-based shell with the AWS CLI already set up, without installing anything locally. What should it use?
questions.correct_rationale: CloudShell is a browser-based shell, pre-authenticated with your console credentials and preloaded with common tools such as the AWS CLI.
questions.distractor_summary: Snowball Edge is a data transfer device, WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops, and Direct Connect is a network link.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: Which option describes connecting an on-premises network to AWS over an encrypted tunnel across the internet?
questions.correct_rationale: Site-to-Site VPN creates IPsec tunnels over the internet between your network and AWS.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct Connect is a dedicated private link rather than an internet tunnel, CloudFront delivers content, and Route 53 Resolver handles DNS.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: A company needs a dedicated, consistent network connection from its data center to AWS that does not go over the public internet. Which service fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private connection with more consistent performance than the internet.
questions.distractor_summary: The VPN options run over the internet, and API Gateway publishes APIs.

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Define methods of deploying and operating in the AWS Cloud
questions.question: What is infrastructure as code?
options: Writing application code on physical servers
Managing and provisioning infrastructure through machine-readable definition files
Using only the console to create resources
questions.correct_rationale: IaC defines infrastructure in files, such as CloudFormation templates, so it can be versioned and repeated.
questions.distractor_summary: The other options are not about defining infrastructure as code.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: What is an AWS Region?
options: A separate geographic area that contains multiple, isolated Availability Zones
A virtual network inside an account
questions.correct_rationale: Each Region is a physical location in the world with multiple Availability Zones.
questions.distractor_summary: A data center is part of an Availability Zone, edge locations cache content, and a VPC is a virtual network.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: What is an Availability Zone?
options: A global network of caching servers
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity in a Region
questions.correct_rationale: Availability Zones are isolated locations within a Region, designed so a failure in one does not affect the others.
questions.distractor_summary: Countries, caching networks, and billing groups are different concepts.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: A company wants its web application to keep running if one data center fails. What is the best practice?
options: Deploy all resources in one Availability Zone with larger instances
Deploy resources across at least two Availability Zones
Deploy in one Availability Zone and take daily snapshots
questions.correct_rationale: Spreading resources across multiple AZs keeps the application available if one AZ has a problem.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger instances in one AZ share the same failure, edge locations do not run full applications, and snapshots help recovery but not continuous availability.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: Which factors should a company consider when choosing an AWS Region?
options: The number of employees at AWS in that country
Whether the Region has a name the company likes
Data residency rules, latency to users, service availability, and price
The color of the console in that Region
questions.correct_rationale: Compliance, proximity, available services, and cost all differ by Region.
questions.distractor_summary: The other factors have no effect on the decision.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: What are AWS edge locations mainly used for?
options: Caching and delivering content with low latency through services such as Amazon CloudFront and Route 53
questions.correct_rationale: Edge locations are points of presence that serve cached content and DNS responses close to users.
questions.distractor_summary: Databases, archives, and Organizations run in Regions, not edge locations.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: Which AWS infrastructure option places compute and storage closer to large cities to give single-digit millisecond latency for specific applications?
questions.correct_rationale: Local Zones extend a Region into metro areas so latency-sensitive workloads can run closer to users.
questions.distractor_summary: Regions may be farther away, Glacier Deep Archive is archival storage, and Artifact holds reports.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: A telecom company wants to run applications at the edge of 5G networks for ultra-low-latency mobile experiences. Which AWS offering is designed for this?
options: AWS Outposts in a single data center
questions.correct_rationale: Wavelength embeds AWS compute and storage in telecommunications providers' 5G networks.
questions.distractor_summary: Outposts brings AWS on premises, CloudFront Functions run lightweight code at edge locations, and Global Accelerator improves routing but does not host apps in 5G networks.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: Which AWS offering runs AWS infrastructure and services in a customer's own data center?
questions.correct_rationale: Outposts are AWS-managed racks or servers installed on premises for low latency or local data processing.
questions.distractor_summary: Local Zones and Wavelength are AWS-run locations, and Lightsail is a simplified cloud service.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: A company stores data in one Region and wants a copy in another Region for disaster recovery. Which statement is accurate?
options: AWS automatically copies all data to every Region
Data cannot leave the Region where it was created
The company must set up replication or backups to the second Region, because AWS does not copy data across Regions automatically for most services
Only edge locations can store copies of data
questions.correct_rationale: Data generally stays in the Region you choose unless you configure cross-Region replication or backups.
questions.distractor_summary: AWS does not replicate data everywhere by default, cross-Region copies are possible when configured, and edge locations are caches.

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Define the AWS global infrastructure
questions.question: Why are Availability Zones in a Region connected with low-latency links?
options: So that every AZ shares the same power supply
So applications can replicate data and fail over between AZs with little delay
So that data automatically moves to other Regions
So that customers do not need to choose a Region
questions.correct_rationale: High-bandwidth, low-latency networking lets synchronous replication and failover work across AZs.
questions.distractor_summary: AZs have independent power, data does not move Regions automatically, and Region choice is still needed.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: Which AWS service provides resizable virtual servers in the cloud?
questions.correct_rationale: EC2 offers virtual machines called instances that you can launch and size as needed.
questions.distractor_summary: S3 is object storage, RDS is a managed database, and Route 53 is DNS.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: A company wants to run code in response to file uploads without managing any servers and pay only for the time the code runs. Which service fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: Lambda runs code in response to events and charges by requests and duration.
questions.distractor_summary: EC2 and Lightsail run servers you manage, and Outposts brings hardware on premises.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: Which EC2 instance family type is best suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases?
questions.correct_rationale: Memory optimized instances provide high memory relative to vCPU for workloads that process large data sets in memory.
questions.distractor_summary: Compute optimized favors CPU, storage optimized favors local disk I/O, and accelerated computing uses GPUs or other accelerators.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: A team wants to run containers without managing the servers or clusters underneath. Which option fits best?
options: AWS Fargate with Amazon ECS or Amazon EKS
questions.correct_rationale: Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers, so you do not provision or manage servers.
questions.distractor_summary: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers, Snowball Edge is an edge device, and EMR runs big data frameworks.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: Which AWS service is a managed Kubernetes service?
questions.correct_rationale: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service runs the Kubernetes control plane for you.
questions.distractor_summary: ECS is AWS's own container orchestrator, Batch runs batch jobs, and Lightsail offers simple virtual servers.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: A small business wants a simple virtual private server with a fixed monthly price for a WordPress site. Which service fits best?
questions.correct_rationale: Lightsail offers easy-to-use virtual servers and bundles with predictable monthly pricing.
questions.distractor_summary: EKS, Batch, and EMR are for containers, batch jobs, and big data.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: Which service automatically adds or removes EC2 instances based on demand?
questions.correct_rationale: EC2 Auto Scaling adjusts the number of instances to match demand or schedules.
questions.distractor_summary: Load balancers distribute traffic, CloudFront caches content, and Config tracks configuration.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: A company runs a web tier on several EC2 instances and needs traffic spread across healthy instances in multiple Availability Zones. Which service should it use?
questions.correct_rationale: Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic across healthy targets in multiple AZs.
questions.distractor_summary: Domain registration, Direct Connect, and Transfer Acceleration do not balance traffic across instances.

questions.subdomain: 3.3 Identify AWS compute services
questions.question: Which EC2 instance family is best for a high-performance web server that is CPU-bound?
questions.correct_rationale: Compute optimized instances offer high-performance processors for CPU-heavy workloads.
questions.distractor_summary: Memory and storage optimized families target other bottlenecks, and burstable instances suit low average CPU use.

questions.subdomain: 3.4 Identify AWS database services
questions.question: Which AWS service provides managed relational databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server?
questions.correct_rationale: Amazon RDS manages common relational database engines, including backups and patching.
questions.distractor_summary: DynamoDB is NoSQL, ElastiCache is in-memory caching, and Neptune is a graph database.

questions.subdomain: 3.4 Identify AWS database services
questions.question: An application needs a serverless key-value database with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon Aurora Serverless with joins across many tables
questions.correct_rationale: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL key-value and document database built for consistent low latency at scale.
questions.distractor_summary: RDS and Aurora are relational, and Redshift is a data warehouse for analytics.

questions.subdomain: 3.4 Identify AWS database services
questions.question: Which AWS database is MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible and built for higher performance and availability than standard engines?
questions.correct_rationale: Aurora is a cloud-native relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.
